# LinkEDA releases

## macOS 0.0.120

LinkEDA 0.0.120 consolidates the recent macOS work on shared analysis scopes,
linked selections, model refitting, statistical interpretation, export and
plot interaction. It is available for Apple Silicon Macs running macOS 14 or
later.

### Highlights

- Analysis scopes, saved selections and exclusions update compatible plots and
  analyses consistently, with controls for keeping a particular view frozen.
- Model diagnostics and post-hoc analyses remain linked to their source model
  and active scope.
- Plot, table and model exports use a common Copy, Save and R Code structure,
  with improved PDF and APA-style output.
- Plot annotations and stickers retain their placement in snapshots and
  exported files.
- Clustering adds distance choices and access to the distance matrix.
- The macOS point-size control is available again for scatterplots, trellis
  plots, scatterplot matrices and PCA plots.
- Three macOS downloads are provided: a standalone application, an application
  using an installed R, and a binary R package for current R users.

The application installers are ad-hoc signed for internal integrity but are
not yet signed with an Apple Developer ID or notarised by Apple. Their
installation cards explain the one-time approval through **System Settings >
Privacy & Security**. The R binary package is installed from R or RStudio and
does not require that approval.

[Download LinkEDA 0.0.120 for macOS](getting-started.qmd#download){.button .button-primary}

## macOS 0.0.119

LinkEDA 0.0.119 is the first downloadable native macOS installer build. It is
available for Apple Silicon Macs running macOS 14 or later.

### Highlights

- A standalone installer with a private R 4.6 runtime.
- A smaller installer that uses an existing Apple Silicon R 4.6 installation.
- A precompiled R package for users who prefer to start LinkEDA from R or
  RStudio.
- Both editions include the R packages used by the application, exact LinkEDA
  source archives and third-party notices.
- Native linked data sheets, plots, scopes, model windows, export and example
  data in a normal Applications-folder installation.

The application is ad-hoc signed for internal integrity. The two application
installers are not yet signed with an Apple Developer ID or notarised by Apple.
The download page explains their one-time approval through **System Settings >
Privacy & Security**. The R binary package is installed from R or RStudio and
does not require that approval.

[Download the macOS installers](getting-started.qmd#download){.button .button-primary}

## Windows v0.0.113R

`v0.0.113R` identifies the first public Windows release. The R package and
application use the numeric functional version `0.0.113`; the final `R` is the
publication marker for the build made available to other users.

### Highlights

- Two double-click Windows installers: a complete edition with a private R
  runtime and a smaller edition for users who already have R.
- Native linked data sheets, plots, selections, explicit case exclusions and
  immutable analysis scopes.
- Linear, binary, count, positive-continuous, proportion, scale,
  dimensionality, missing-data and multiple-imputation workflows calculated in R.
- Shared R verification recipes and publication exports.

[Download the Windows installers](getting-started.qmd#windows){.button .button-primary}

## Licensing and verification

Binary installers are attached to GitHub Releases instead of being committed
to the source repository. Checksums are published on the download page. The
software is distributed under GPL version 3 or later; original published
documentation uses CC BY-NC-ND 4.0.
